learning_objective: 🎯 Understand what makes writing truly creative! Learn how to tap into your imagination, overcome writer's block, and express your unique voice.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Creativity is the ability to generate new, original, and valuable ideas. In writing, it means looking at ordinary things in an extraordinary way and putting your personal spin on them.

Good writing doesn't happen magically in one try. It involves several stages: Brainstorming (gathering ideas), Drafting (writing them down), Revising (improving the flow), and Editing (fixing grammar).

Writer's block is the terrifying feeling of staring at a blank page with no ideas. You can beat it by 'freewriting' (writing continuously without stopping to correct mistakes) or taking a walk to refresh your mind.
Your 'voice' is your unique style as a writer. It is how your personality shines through your words—whether you are funny, serious, poetic, or sarcastic.

fun_activity.title: ⏱️ The 5-Minute Freewrite
fun_activity.instructions: Set a timer for exactly 5 minutes. Start writing about a 'purple umbrella' and DO NOT stop. Even if you don't know what to write, type 'I don't know what to write' until a new idea comes. No erasing allowed! This unlocks your creative flow.

exam_tips: 📌 Always outline the 'Stages of the Writing Process' clearly: Pre-writing, Drafting, Revising, Editing, and Publishing.
📌 Use examples when defining 'creativity'. Show how it differs from academic or technical writing.
📌 Know 3-4 practical techniques to overcome Writer's Block (e.g., changing environment, reading prompts, freewriting).
quick_recap: ⭐ Creative writing relies on imagination and personal expression, not just facts.
⭐ The writing process is recursive, meaning you can jump back and forth between drafting and editing.
⭐ Writer's block is natural and can be defeated with continuous, unedited writing exercises.
